title: He lied.
paragraphs:
He lied.
He ran.
He thought he got away with it.
But you can’t outrun what’s inside you.

Jacob carried it into the night—
the deception,
the stolen blessing,
the echo of his brother’s fury chasing him through the dark.

No audience.
No altar.
No worship music.

Just a man…
and a stone for a pillow.

And right there—
at his lowest, most undeserving moment—
heaven broke through.
Genesis 28 tells us Jacob lay down to sleep in the wilderness, vulnerable, exposed, with nothing but fear and consequence surrounding him.
This was not a holy man in a holy place.
A son who betrayed his own blood.

A ladder—set on the earth,
its top reaching into heaven.

Angels ascending and descending—
movement, activity, access.
And above it stood the LORD.
Let that settle into your bones.

God didn’t wait for Jacob to fix himself.
He didn’t say, “Come back when you’re clean.”
He didn’t cancel the promise because of the failure.

“I am the LORD…
I am with you…
I will keep you…
I will not leave you…” (Genesis 28:13–15)
The one who pretended to be someone else just to steal what wasn’t his.

And God responds with…
covenant.
Presence.
Promise.

Because religion says:
“Climb your way up. Earn your place. Fix your mess.”

Still broken.
Still guilty.
Still running.
The ladder was not Jacob reaching heaven.
Some scholars interpret this ladder as a visible sign of God’s active involvement between heaven and earth—His initiative, not man’s effort. A divine bridge, not a human achievement.
And centuries later, Jesus steps into the scene and says something that unlocks everything:
“You will see heaven open, and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man.” (John 1:51)
He was pointing back to Jacob’s dream.
But He wasn’t just explaining it.

Not wood.
Not steps.
Not a structure you climb.
The only connection between a holy God and broken humanity.
You don’t ascend to God by effort.
You are reconciled to Him through Christ.

Through His life.
His cross.
His resurrection.
Some of you reading this… you feel like Jacob.
You’ve done things you can’t undo.
You’ve worn masks to get ahead.
And now you’re running—maybe not physically, but internally.

Running from guilt.
From exposure.
From the quiet voice that won’t let you rest.
And here’s the shock of grace:

Right there—
in the middle of the mess.
“Surely the LORD is in this place, and I did not know it.” (Genesis 28:16)
You may feel far from God.
But distance in your heart does not equal absence in His presence.
Jesus didn’t wait for you to climb.
He stepped into our dust, our sin, our chaos—
and then He went to the cross.
That’s where the ladder was secured forever.

Where heaven touched earth…
and mercy outran judgment.

You are more sinful than you want to admit.
And more loved than you can comprehend.
So what do you do with this?
You stop trying to earn what has already been offered.
Jacob laid his head on a stone in guilt…

and woke up in a place he later called Bethel—
“the house of God.”
Heaven is not closed to you.

Not with polished words.
Not with perfect behavior.
And watch what God does with a life that thought it was too far gone.
Someone you know is running in the dark tonight.
